# `PIXterm` - *draw images in your ANSI terminal with true color*

**`PIXterm`** ***shows images directly in your terminal***, recreating the pixels through a combination of [ANSI character background color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Colors) and the [unicode lower half block element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements). If image has transparency, an optional matte color can be used for background. Also, you can specify a dithering mode; in which case, the image is rendered using block elements with different shades, or using standard ASCII characters in the same way. In dithering mode, the matte color is used to fill the background of the blocks or characters.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.

Fetching images from HTTP/HTTPS is supported too.

## Usage

```
pixterm [options] <image file or URL>
```

### Options

- `-version` - show PIXterm version
- `-credits` - show some love to contributors <3
- `-d <mode>` - dithering mode:
  - `0` - no dithering (default)
  - `1` - with blocks
  - `2` - with chars
- `-go` - output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image
- `-m <color>` - matte color for transparency or background (optional, hex format, default: 000000)
- `-nobg` - disable background color (optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)
- `-s <method>` - scale method:
  - `0` - resize (default)
  - `1` - fill
  - `2` - fit
- `-tr <rows>` - terminal rows (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)
- `-tc <columns>` - terminal columns (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)

## Requirements

Your terminal emulator must support *true color* in order to display image colors correctly. In addition, you must use a monospaced font that includes the lower half block unicode character: `▄ (U+2584)`. [Envy Code R](https://damieng.com/blog/2008/05/26/envy-code-r-preview-7-coding-font-released) is recommended. If you want to use the dithering mode with blocks, the font must also include the following unicode characters: `█ (U+2588)`, `▓ (U+2593)`, `▒ (U+2592)`, `░ (U+2591)`. The dithering mode with characters works with standard ASCII chars.

data=open("/tmp/dither_blocks.txt","rb").read()
# Each cell is: ESC[48;2;R;G;Bm ESC[38;2;R;G;Bm CHAR ESC[0m? Actually per cell: bg + fg + char, rows end with ESC[0m\n
# For dither blocks, bg is matte (0,0,0), fg is gray, char varies.
# Let's parse first row
import re
# Split by rows (ESC[0m\n)
rows=data.split(b"\x1b[0m\n")
print(f"num rows: {len(rows)} first row len: {len(rows[0])}")
# Parse cells in first row: pattern ESC[48;2;...m ESC[38;2;...m CHAR
# CHAR can be 1 byte (space) or 3 bytes (utf8 block)
# Let's use regex
pat=re.compile(br"\x1b\[48;2;(\d+);(\d+);(\d+)m\x1b\[38;2;(\d+);(\d+);(\d+)m(.)")
# But . won't match multibyte? Use separate
# Instead split manually
row=rows[0]
# Find all bg/fg
# Use re for bg/fg then char is next bytes until next ESC
cells=re.findall(br"\x1b\[48;2;(\d+);(\d+);(\d+)m\x1b\[38;2;(\d+);(\d+);(\d+)m([^\x1b]*)", row)
print(f"num cells first row: {len(cells)}")
for i,(br,bg,bb,fr,fg,fb,ch) in enumerate(cells):
    print(f"{i}: fg={fr.decode()},{fg.decode()},{fb.decode()} char={ch!r} hex={ch.hex()}")
PY"}

# `PIXterm` - *draw images in your ANSI terminal with true color*

**`PIXterm`** ***shows images directly in your terminal***, recreating the pixels through a combination of [ANSI character background color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Colors) and the [unicode lower half block element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements). If image has transparency, an optional matte color can be used for background. Also, you can specify a dithering mode; in which case, the image is rendered using block elements with different shades, or using standard ASCII characters in the same way. In dithering mode, the matte color is used to fill the background of the blocks or characters.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.

Fetching images from HTTP/HTTPS is supported too.

## Usage

```
pixterm [options] <image file or URL>

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"image"
	_ "image/gif"
	_ "image/jpeg"
	_ "image/png"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
	"syscall"
	"unsafe"
)

const versionStr = "1.3.2
"

const logoStr = "   ___  _____  ____
  / _ \/  _/ |/_/ /____ ______ _      Made with love by Eliuk Blau
 / ___// /_>  </ __/ -_) __/  ' \ https://github.com/eliukblau/pixterm
/_/  /___/_/|_|\__/\__/_/ /_/_/_/                1.3.2

"

const creditsStr = "CONTRIBUTORS:

  > @disq - https://github.com/disq
      + Original code for image transparency support.

  > @timob - https://github.com/timob
      + Fix for ANSIpixel type: use 8bit color component for output.

  > @HongjiangHuang - https://github.com/HongjiangHuang
      + Original code for image download support.

  > @brutestack - https://github.com/brutestack
      + Color support for Windows (Command Prompt & PowerShell).
      + Original code for disable background color in dithering mode.
      + Original code for output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image.

  > @diamondburned - https://github.com/diamondburned
      + NewFromImage() & NewScaledFromImage() for ANSImage API.

  > @MichaelMure - https://github.com/MichaelMure
      + More conventional 'go.mod' file at repository.

  > @Calinou - https://github.com/Calinou
      + Use HTTPS URLs everywhere.
      + Other awesome contributions.

  > @danirod - https://github.com/danirod
  > @Xpktro - https://github.com/Xpktro
      + Moral support.

"

func printLogoAndUsage() {
	prog := filepath.Base(os.Args[0])
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, logoStr)
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "USAGE:

  %s [options] image/url

  Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.
  Supported URL protocols: HTTP, HTTPS.

OPTIONS:

  -credits
    	show some love to contributors <3
  -d mode
    	dithering mode:
    	   0 - no dithering (default)
    	   1 - with blocks
    	   2 - with chars
  -go
    	output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image
  -m color
    	matte color for transparency or background
    	(optional, hex format, default: 000000)
  -nobg
    	disable background color
    	(optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)
  -s method
    	scale method:
    	   0 - resize (default)
    	   1 - fill
    	   2 - fit
  -tc columns
    	terminal columns (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)
  -tr rows
    	terminal rows (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)
  -version
    	show PIXterm version
  -help
	prints this message :D LOL

")
}

func printLogo() {
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, logoStr)
